case.display_title: Transferred with very low blood counts

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on severe pancytopenia in a woman transferred as possible aplastic anaemia. We reviewed the Chart so far. The counts are profoundly low with a normal MCV, but one unit of red cells was given before transfer, so the indices are hard to interpret. The differential is wide: marrow failure, a myeloid neoplasm or infiltrate, a nutritional deficiency such as vitamin B12, folate or copper, drugs and infection. Nutritional causes need to be excluded early because they are reversible. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Send serum vitamin B12, folate and copper, and iron studies, before further transfusion where possible
Reticulocyte count, LDH and a blood film reviewed by a haematopathologist
Take a full nutritional, surgical and medicine history, including supplements
Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with flow cytometry, cytogenetics and molecular studies
Continue empirical antimicrobials for neutropenia; transfuse platelets for bleeding or below 10 x10^9/L

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes a marrow with increased blasts and trilineage dysplasia. On morphology alone this could fit a high-grade myelodysplastic neoplasm. However, the erythroid precursors show megaloblastic change, and severe vitamin B12 or folate depletion, copper deficiency, drugs and infection can all produce dysplasia and a transient rise in blasts. We would not make a diagnosis of a myeloid neoplasm, or start disease-directed treatment, until the haematinics, cytogenetics and molecular results are back. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Chase serum vitamin B12, folate and copper urgently
Await karyotype, FISH, SNP microarray and the myeloid NGS panel
No hypomethylating or induction chemotherapy at this stage
Supportive care: antimicrobials, platelet and red cell transfusion as needed

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes a serum folate of 2.6 ng/mL with vitamin B12 above 1500 pg/mL. Folate at this level can produce megaloblastic trilineage dysplasia, a hypocellular or left-shifted marrow and a transient increase in blasts that resembles a myelodysplastic neoplasm. After a sleeve gastrectomy with poor intake, stores run out within months. We recommend folate replacement with supportive care, and interpreting the marrow again once the cytogenetic and molecular results are available and the counts have had time to respond. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Oral folic acid 5 mg daily (intravenous if oral absorption is in doubt), having confirmed that vitamin B12 is replete
Full blood count and reticulocytes every two to three days; expect a reticulocyte response within a week
Repeat bone marrow after two to three weeks of replacement to confirm that the blasts and dysplasia resolve
No cytotoxic or hypomethylating treatment
Dietetic review and long-term bariatric vitamin supplementation

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to assess nutrition. She had a sleeve gastrectomy and now manages only small amounts of soft food, with very little fruit or vegetables; she stopped the daily multivitamin advised after the operation about a year ago. She has lost about 8 kg in the past year and her BMI is 19.4. Intake of protein and of several micronutrients is likely to be poor. She is at risk of refeeding problems. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Micronutrient screen after bariatric surgery: folate, vitamin B12, iron studies, vitamin D, zinc, copper and thiamine
Thiamine before increasing feeding; monitor phosphate, magnesium and potassium daily for the first few days
High-protein oral nutritional supplements in small, frequent portions
Restart a complete bariatric multivitamin and mineral supplement for life once acute issues settle

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes a serum folate of 2.6 ng/mL. With a sleeve gastrectomy, a diet with very little fruit or vegetables and no supplement for a year, a very low folate is expected. Replacement is for the medical team; our role is to rebuild intake and prevent recurrence. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Folate-rich foods she can manage: soft cooked lentils and beans, green vegetables in soups, fortified cereals
High-protein oral nutritional supplements in small, frequent portions
Refeeding monitoring as before
A complete bariatric multivitamin and mineral supplement for life, with annual micronutrient checks

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on antimicrobials in profound neutropenia. We reviewed the Chart so far. She is on cefepime, metronidazole and fluconazole, started for presumed colitis and mucositis; the diarrhoea is settling and the abdomen is soft. The lymphocyte count is also very low, which raises the risk of opportunistic infection, including Pneumocystis. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Continue cefepime while neutropenic; add cover if she becomes febrile or unstable
Stop metronidazole if C. difficile testing and stool cultures are negative and the diarrhoea has settled
Blood cultures with any fever; low threshold for CT chest if respiratory symptoms or oxygen requirement develop
Check a CD4 count and consider Pneumocystis prophylaxis once the platelet and neutrophil counts allow
The marrow picture is for haematology; infection alone does not explain it

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on diarrhoea and nutrition. We reviewed the Chart so far. The loose stools are settling and the abdomen is soft; with neutrophils this low and platelets below 6 x10^9/L, endoscopy is not safe or needed now. After a sleeve gastrectomy, reduced intake and non-adherence to supplements are the usual reasons for micronutrient deficiency rather than a new gut disease. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Stool culture and C. difficile testing
Micronutrient screen, including folate, vitamin B12, iron, zinc, copper and vitamin D
No endoscopy while the counts are this low
Dietetic input

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to review. She had a sleeve gastrectomy some years ago. There is no sign of a surgical complication: the abdomen is soft and non-tender. After a sleeve, small meals, early satiety and stopping the recommended supplements commonly lead to deficiencies of iron, vitamin B12, folate, vitamin D, zinc and copper. No surgical intervention is needed. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Full post-bariatric micronutrient screen
Lifelong bariatric multivitamin and mineral supplement, with vitamin B12 as she already has
Dietetic follow-up; bariatric clinic follow-up after discharge

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about treatment for a possible myeloid neoplasm. We reviewed the Chart so far. Myeloid neoplasms are managed by haematology here. Before any hypomethylating or intensive treatment we would need a confirmed diagnosis, with cytogenetic and molecular results, and reversible causes of dysplasia excluded. We would not start treatment on the current information. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Discuss with haematology
Await cytogenetics, FISH, SNP microarray and NGS
Supportive care in the meantime

consult_notes.note_text: Asked whether an autoimmune disease could explain the pancytopenia. We reviewed the Chart so far. She has no joint, skin or other features of a connective tissue disease. If the autoimmune screen is negative, we have nothing further to add. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: ANA, anti-dsDNA, complement and rheumatoid factor if not already sent
Direct antiglobulin test

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to review hypothyroidism after total thyroidectomy. We reviewed the Chart so far. Hypothyroidism can contribute to a mild anaemia but does not cause pancytopenia of this degree. Absorption of levothyroxine can change after bariatric surgery. Happy to review again with the results.

Continue levothyroxine at the current dose if TSH is in range

ground_truth.outcome: Cytopenias normalised over 18 days of folate. A repeat marrow at that time was 60% cellular with myeloid-predominant haematopoiesis, mild dysmegakaryopoiesis and 1% blasts. The findings were judged an unusual reactive process due to folate deficiency.

KMT2A variant of uncertain significance at 49.6% VAF
the referral label of aplastic anaemia

rubric.text: Folate deficiency, with the sleeve gastrectomy or poor intake identified as the cause

teaching_points: Severe folate or B12 deficiency can produce trilineage dysplasia and a transient rise in blasts that looks like a high-grade myelodysplastic neoplasm or AML.
Check haematinics (B12, folate, copper) before labelling a myeloid neoplasm, particularly after bariatric surgery or with malnutrition.
Blasts without an aberrant immunophenotype and a normal karyotype, FISH and SNP array argue against a clonal disorder; a low-VAF DNMT3A variant can be clonal haematopoiesis.
Folate stores last only months; after a sleeve gastrectomy, poor intake and stopped supplements deplete them quickly, while B12 injections can keep the B12 level normal.
Macrocytosis can be absent after transfusion or with coexisting conditions.
Recovery of the counts and marrow after replacement confirms the diagnosis.
ground_truth.treatment_given: Folate supplementation (dose not reported) with supportive care: red cell transfusion and antimicrobials for neutropenia. Pneumocystis pneumonia on day 3 needed intubation.

raw_material.findings: Red cells with minimal anisopoikilocytosis. Eosinophils increased (50% of leucocytes) with frequent atypical nuclear segmentation. Rare hypogranular neutrophils.
Eosinophils increased (54% of viable leucocytes); myeloid blasts slightly increased (1.5% of viable leucocytes); no abnormal B-cell, T-cell, NK-cell or mast cell populations.

Erythroid-predominant trilineage haematopoiesis; 12% blasts and 15% eosinophils by morphology; dyserythropoiesis and dysmegakaryopoiesis. Erythroid maturation left-shifted with increased pronormoblasts and basophilic normoblasts; frequent erythroid precursors with megaloblastic changes, cytoplasmic vacuolisation, nuclear contour irregularities, nuclear budding, macronuclei and multinucleation. Frequent small hypolobate megakaryocytes, megakaryocytes with hyperlobate nuclei and with widely spaced nuclear lobes. Granulocytes with a prominent left shift; blasts with amphophilic to basophilic cytoplasm, high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, immature chromatin, variably prominent nucleoli and sparse red granules. Occasional histiocytes with haemophagocytosis. Pathologists' reading: highly suspicious for MDS-IB2 (WHO 5th edition) or MDS/AML (ICC 2022).
Increased storage iron; adequate sideroblastic iron; no ring sideroblasts.

Marrow cellularity about 20% on H&E (the text also calls the core normocellular; the caption and the opening sentence give 20%). CD34: increased myeloid blasts, about 15% of cellularity. CD61: increased megakaryocytes, many small, with atypical nuclear features. E-cadherin: increased immature erythroid precursors including megaloblastic forms.

Myeloid blasts 18% of viable leucocytes without immunophenotypic aberrancy: positive for CD34, CD13, CD33, CD38, CD117, CD123, HLA-DR and MPO; negative for CD3, CD5, CD7, CD10, CD14, CD19, CD56, CD64 and TdT. Eosinophils 45% of viable leucocytes.
No abnormalities; not supportive of a myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and a tyrosine kinase gene fusion.

reports.impression: Pancytopenia with a relative eosinophilia; rare hypogranular neutrophils.
reports.report_text: Marked leucopenia. Eosinophils make up about half of the leucocytes, and many show atypical nuclear segmentation. Neutrophils are very scanty; rare hypogranular forms are seen. Red cells show minimal anisopoikilocytosis. Platelets are markedly reduced.

reports.impression: Pancytopenia with a relative eosinophilia and hypogranular neutrophils.
reports.report_text: Film reviewed by a haematopathologist. Severe leucopenia with very few neutrophils, some of them hypogranular. Eosinophils make up about half of the leucocytes; many show atypical nuclear segmentation, but the absolute eosinophil count is not raised. Red cells show minimal anisopoikilocytosis; a transfused population may contribute. Platelets are markedly reduced with no clumps. No circulating blasts identified on this film. Comment: in pancytopenia with dysplastic neutrophils, suggest serum vitamin B12, folate and copper, and a bone marrow examination with cytogenetics if the cause is not found.
reports.status_line: Final report, reviewed by a haematopathologist.

reports.impression: Relative eosinophilia; slight increase in circulating myeloid blasts (1.5%); no abnormal lymphoid or mast cell population.
reports.report_text: Peripheral blood. Eosinophils are increased, making up 54% of viable leucocytes. Myeloid blasts are slightly increased at 1.5% of viable leucocytes. No abnormal B-cell, T-cell, NK-cell or mast cell population is identified.

reports.impression: Trilineage dysplasia with megaloblastic erythroid change and increased blasts (12%); occasional haemophagocytosis.
reports.report_text: Aspirate with erythroid-predominant trilineage haematopoiesis. Blasts 12% and eosinophils 15% on the differential count. Erythropoiesis is left-shifted, with increased pronormoblasts and basophilic normoblasts; many erythroid precursors show megaloblastic change, cytoplasmic vacuolation, irregular nuclear contours, nuclear budding, macronuclei or multinucleation. Megakaryocytes include frequent small hypolobate forms, forms with hyperlobate nuclei and forms with widely separated nuclear lobes. Granulopoiesis shows a prominent left shift; the blasts have amphophilic to basophilic cytoplasm, a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, immature chromatin, variably prominent nucleoli and sparse red granules. Occasional histiocytes show haemophagocytosis. See the iron stain, trephine and flow cytometry reports. Comment: the findings are highly suspicious for a myelodysplastic neoplasm with increased blasts; correlation with cytogenetic and molecular studies is recommended.

reports.impression: Increased storage iron; no ring sideroblasts.
reports.report_text: Perls stain on the aspirate. Storage iron is increased in the marrow fragments. Sideroblastic iron is adequate. No ring sideroblasts are seen.

reports.impression: Hypocellular marrow (about 20%) with increased CD34-positive blasts (about 15%), dysplastic megakaryocytes and increased immature erythroid precursors.
reports.report_text: Trephine core. Cellularity about 20%, reduced for age. Immunohistochemistry: CD34 highlights increased myeloid blasts, about 15% of the cellularity; CD61 shows increased megakaryocytes, including many small forms and forms with atypical nuclei; E-cadherin shows increased immature erythroid precursors, including megaloblastic forms. No significant reticulin fibrosis. No granulomas or non-haemopoietic infiltrate.

reports.impression: Increased myeloid blasts (18%) without a definite aberrant immunophenotype; eosinophils increased.
reports.report_text: Bone marrow aspirate. Myeloid blasts are increased at 18% of viable leucocytes. They express CD34, CD13, CD33, CD38, CD117, CD123, HLA-DR and MPO, and are negative for CD3, CD5, CD7, CD10, CD14, CD19, CD56, CD64 and TdT. No definite immunophenotypic aberrancy is detected. Eosinophils are increased at 45% of viable leucocytes.

reports.impression: Normal female karyotype, 46,XX.
reports.report_text: Twenty metaphases analysed at a 400-band level. Karyotype 46,XX. No clonal abnormality detected.

reports.impression: Normal MDS FISH panel.
reports.report_text: Two hundred interphase nuclei scored per probe. Normal signal patterns for 5q31, 7q31, the chromosome 8 centromere and 20q12; no deletion or gain detected.

reports.impression: Normal AML FISH panel.
reports.report_text: Two hundred interphase nuclei scored per probe. No RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, PML::RARA or KMT2A rearrangement, and no loss of 5q, 7q or 17p (TP53) detected.

reports.impression: Normal eosinophilia FISH panel.
reports.report_text: Two hundred interphase nuclei scored per probe. No FIP1L1::PDGFRA fusion (CHIC2 deletion) and no PDGFRB, FGFR1 or JAK2 rearrangement detected.

reports.impression: Normal SNP microarray.
reports.report_text: Genome-wide cytogenomic SNP microarray on the marrow specimen. No clinically significant copy number alteration or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity detected.

reports.impression: No targetable AML mutation detected.
reports.report_text: Rapid targeted next-generation sequencing for AML therapy targets, including FLT3 (internal tandem duplication and tyrosine kinase domain), IDH1, IDH2 and NPM1. No mutation detected.

reports.impression: Low-level DNMT3A variant (VAF 1.2%); KMT2A variant of uncertain significance (VAF 49.6%).
reports.report_text: Myeloid malignancies mutation and copy number panel by next-generation sequencing, adequate coverage. Tier 1 variant: DNMT3A, variant allele frequency 1.2%. Variant of uncertain clinical significance (reported as Tier 2): KMT2A, variant allele frequency 49.6%; a frequency near 50% may indicate a constitutional variant. No other variants or copy number changes detected. Comment: a low-level DNMT3A variant can be found in clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential; interpret with the morphology and cytogenetics.

reports.impression: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
reports.report_text: PA erect chest radiograph. The heart size and mediastinal contours are normal. The lungs are clear and the costophrenic angles are sharp. Surgical clips project over the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.

reports.impression: Faint bilateral upper-lobe ground-glass opacity, non-specific; in a neutropenic patient an early infection cannot be excluded.
reports.report_text: CT of the chest. Faint patchy ground-glass opacity in both upper lobes. No consolidation, nodules, cavitation or interstitial thickening. The airways are patent. No mediastinal or hilar lymph node enlargement and no pleural or pericardial fluid. In the upper abdomen, a narrow tubular stomach with a staple line.

reports.impression: Sleeve gastrectomy. No colitis, collection or splenomegaly.
reports.report_text: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis in the portal venous phase. Post-surgical appearance of a sleeve gastrectomy with an intact staple line and no leak or collection. The liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys are normal; the spleen is not enlarged. The bowel is of normal calibre with no wall thickening. No lymph node enlargement, free fluid or free gas.

reports.impression: Normal abdominal ultrasound; spleen not enlarged.
reports.report_text: The liver is normal in size and echotexture with no focal lesion. The gallbladder is thin-walled without calculi and the common bile duct is not dilated. The spleen measures 10 cm and is homogeneous. Both kidneys, the pancreas and the aorta appear normal. No free fluid.

reports.impression: Appearance after sleeve gastrectomy; no ulceration or source of bleeding; normal duodenal histology.
reports.report_text: Endoscopy to the second part of the duodenum. Normal oesophagus. Post-surgical tubular stomach after sleeve gastrectomy with an intact staple line; mild patchy erythema of the gastric mucosa without ulceration. Normal duodenal mucosa. No bleeding. Duodenal biopsies: normal villous architecture.

reports.impression: Post-thyroidectomy appearance; no mass or lymphadenopathy.
reports.report_text: Thyroidectomy bed: no residual thyroid tissue or mass. No enlarged or morphologically abnormal cervical lymph nodes. The salivary glands appear normal.
